decisions_log.decision: Increment 1 SHIPPED, committed and MERGED to main -- the requirements record splits into a live contract and an append-only ledger, and V26 enforces the split
decisions_log.notes: s19_app dde935c (2026-08-29 12:07:14 -0600), merged 81 seconds later as PR #204, merge commit 1238b7e. THIS IS THE ONLY batch-89 COMMIT ON origin/main; the other two are pushed on claude/batch-89-lean-contract and unmerged (git log origin/main..HEAD). Flow repos: ~/.claude 8438000 (rev48), skills mirror a05a291. V26 checks three things: a 54,000-char budget over the live contract that EXCLUDES the ledger (NOTICE, never BLOCK), a paragraph-bounded Markdown strikethrough check that is deliberately NOT a vocabulary guard (R-88-16), and a both-ways comparison of (requirement, entry) PAIRS -- PAIR-crossed is the discriminating fixture, identical id sets on both sides with only the pairs swapped, on which every membership oracle reports a clean pass. The budget is not typed: it is (_LEAN_CORPUS_MEDIAN_CHARS // 1000) * 1000, and BUDGET-derivation re-derives the median-floor over five supplied size lists before BUDGET-constant checks the shipped constant IS that derivation. VERIFIED AT THE COMMIT: 431 arms (402 -> 431), 0 fail, SELFTEST PASSED; 23 -> 24 registered rules; --map 24 in table order, 24 agree, 0 differ, 0 missing; gate 2 block (this tree's own uncommitted rows) / 287 notice / 21 n/a; V26 on its own record 26,068 chars inside budget, 10 pairings identical both ways. FOUR SELF-REPORTED DEFECTS, two of them the increment turning on its own author. (a) The budget was DERIVED IN BYTES (os.path.getsize, median 55,367) and ENFORCED IN CHARACTERS (len(), median 54,367), so 55,000 shipped where 54,000 was honest -- a whole flooring step -- and the arm that should have caught it compared the literal 55000 against the literal 55000. It was FLAGGED AS VACUOUS IN THE FIRST DRAFT AND KEPT ANYWAY. LED-89.3 is left standing exactly as written and superseded by name in LED-89.5, because the ledger is append-only. (b) The first arm for the _strip_code fix CALLED _strip_code ITSELF and mutant M19-no-strip-code SURVIVED it -- an arm over a helper is not an arm over the rule, committed inside the arm written to close that very finding. (c) An independent adversarial review found the survivor 'if ledger is None:' -> 'if not ledger:', under which an unreadable ledger arrives as the empty string, silently takes the legacy path, and every BLOCK the rule can raise vanishes; closed by LEDGER-empty-string. (d) The two id grammars diverged on their terminator, so a heading ending in a period made one requirement produce two unequal pairs and one BLOCK state something false; closed by a trailing word boundary and armed by GRAMMAR-agree. THE MUTANT TALLIES IN THE RECORD DO NOT RECONCILE -- 19 mutations / 19 red / 0 survived in the commit message, against 12 named single-edit plus 12 review-scored in FLOW-VERSION rev48 -- and the packet marks the reconciliation ABSENT rather than averaging it. V2 registered VACUOUS on this project and left unrepaired: R-89-6 (it harvests 0 of batch-88's nine AT ids), R-89-7 (it resolves ids against <project>/tests/ alone, while this batch's acceptance arms live in --selftest), R-89-8 (three returned template fields are mandatory and enforced by no rule). Packet: 03-increments/increment-001.md, WRITTEN 2026-08-30, after the fact, and it says so at the top.

decisions_log.decision: Increment 2 SHIPPED and committed -- the selftest states a verdict under any stdout encoding, and the defect was REPRODUCED on two surfaces before a line of the repair was written
decisions_log.notes: s19_app 1d2e9fe (2026-08-29 13:30:47 -0600), which carries two increments TOGETHER and is NOT on origin/main. Flow repos: ~/.claude 51203c7 (rev49), skills mirror 7b84e0c. The work was gated on OBSERVING the defect: premise P-8 was UNDECIDABLE precisely because every run in this batch had PYTHONIOENCODING pinned and therefore avoided the crash rather than seeing it. Both surfaces, taken before any repair: PYTHONIOENCODING unset with stdout redirected -> exit 1, UnicodeEncodeError on U+2212, 12 arm lines on disk, NO VERDICT; PYTHONIOENCODING=ascii -> exit 1 on U+00B7, the separator in every arm line, inside the FIRST arm, 0 arm lines, NO VERDICT. The load-bearing half is the missing verdict: a crash prints zero FAILs and no SELFTEST PASSED, which is indistinguishable from a pass to every consumer reading the exit code alone, in the one mode carrying CI authority. Repaired AT THE STREAM (_harden_streams sets errors=backslashreplace on stdout/stderr at __main__), not at the fixture, because the U+2212 there is one instance of a class: 534 non-cp1252 characters of 28 kinds over the 22 canon rows, and 2,511 non-ASCII of 38 kinds against ASCII. The consumer's ENCODING is deliberately NOT overridden -- forcing utf-8 would trade a loud failure for a quiet corruption. THREE CORRECTIONS TO THE COMMISSIONING BRIEF, all measured against it: the stated cause was block buffering and it is WRONG (Python flushes at shutdown; the cause is the ENCODING, which is why one encoding is not a domain); the '601 non-cp1252 characters of 6 kinds' figure did not reproduce and is most likely a double count of a duplicated tree (canon alone 534 of 28; canon plus the generated bundle mirror 1,310 of 34); and flow-selftest.yml lives in ~/.claude, not in this repository. MEASURED AT THE COMMIT: 443 arms, 0 fail, for both increments together; V26 on the record 27,893 chars inside budget, 15 pairings identical both ways. ABSENT: the split of the +12 arms and of rev49's 13-mutant battery between the two increments was never recorded and cannot be recovered from one commit; so was the gate line. The commit also DELETES project.toml, a stray duplicate of pyproject.toml present since the first commit 8533c72, which belongs to neither increment and is declared as such in the packet. Packet: 03-increments/increment-002.md, WRITTEN 2026-08-30, after the fact.

decisions_log.decision: Increment 3 SHIPPED and committed -- the flow names an interpreter that exists, and V17 EXECUTES the guard's declared interpreter instead of stat-ing it
decisions_log.notes: Same landing commit as the previous entry: s19_app 1d2e9fe, flow ~/.claude 51203c7 (rev49), skills mirror 7b84e0c. NOT on origin/main. python3 on this machine resolves to the Microsoft Store alias in WindowsApps -- a real file, on PATH, that shutil.which reports and os.path.isfile confirms -- which prints 'Python was not found' and EXITS 49 WITHOUT STARTING PYTHON; executing hooks/flow-guard.py through its own shebang exited 49, a silent non-run. V17 could not see it because _guard_path_resolves tested os.path.isfile and stopped, so the gate printed 'SKIP: guard wired on UserPromptSubmit' while every rule the guard enforces went unenforced. 'Resolves' was the wrong verb and the requirement was rewritten to 'starts Python when executed' (LED-89.11); _interpreter_runs now executes the token and reads back a marker. Three shebangs changed to python; flow-selftest.yml:40 KEEPS python3 by ruling, because that job runs on ubuntu-latest and THE RUNNER'S PROVISION OF python WAS NOT MEASURED -- an unmeasured premise is not a licence to change a working CI line -- so the threshold is agreement among the four LOCAL sites and never a global count of zero. The correction had a population and was swept (R-88-17): FLOW-VERSION.md:10 and flow-selftest.yml:57 updated, flow-selftest.yml:40 kept with a comment saying why, FLOW-VERSION.md:202 correctly untouched as historical prose. THREE THINGS THAT WENT WRONG AND ARE NOT SMOOTHED OVER. (a) The lessons catalogue ALREADY CARRIED THIS TRAP and the flow shipped python3 anyway: learning a lesson and encoding it are different acts. (b) The first dead-interpreter fixture was a temp TEXT FILE, so _interpreter_runs refused it from the OSError branch and never evaluated its return expression -- and the mutant replacing that expression with 'return True', WHICH IS THE ORIGINAL DEFECT EXACTLY, SURVIVED the full selftest; closed by INT RUNS!=IS-PYTHON using a real non-Python executable discovered at runtime. (c) A whitespace split mangled the correctly quoted interpreter 'C:/Program Files/Py/python.exe' into 'Files/Py/python.exe', so the NEW V17 would have false-BLOCKed most of Windows on the one rule whose BLOCK stops the flow (C-53); found by INT INTERP-parse failing on its own author's expected value, and closed by _cmd_tokens. AN EARLIER HARNESS RUN HAD A RED BASELINE AND ITS KILLS WERE DISCARDED rather than reported; the reported 13 of 13 were scored against a GREEN baseline. ABSENT: the per-increment arm split, and the gate line at this commit -- neither was recorded. Packet: 03-increments/increment-003.md, WRITTEN 2026-08-30, after the fact.

decisions_log.decision: Increment 6 SHIPPED and committed -- V27 and V28 ship, and the property asked for as 'a batch does not reach main below station P4' is reported UNIMPLEMENTABLE rather than faked
decisions_log.notes: s19_app 686733c (2026-08-30 20:07:13 -0600), NOT on origin/main. Flow repos: ~/.claude 3a2c5eb (rev50), skills mirror 029e441. A SIXTH INCREMENT ON A RECORD THAT DECLARED FIVE: the scope moved through the ledger, LED-89.13 to LED-89.19, by APPENDING the reason and editing the current sentence, never by striking it -- the lean-contract mechanism from the first increment used for the first time on a change it did not anticipate. V27 (NOTICE, selector S1 plus the project repo's commit history) checks coverage as a CORRESPONDENCE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS and currency against the newest commit touching the batch directory, asked of git WITH A PATHSPEC. The harvest reads the decision field and NEVER notes, forced by the real record: batch-88's P0 entry at 0f40624 carries notes naming increments a design review had NOT yet authorised, so a wide harvest reports them LOGGED on the one record the rule exists to have caught. Equality is CURRENT not behind; the newest entry is a MAXIMUM, never log[-1]; git-unaskable and no-commit-yet are two DIFFERENT unchecked states, because the interpreter increment of this same batch already paid for collapsing two causes into one message. V28 (NOTICE, selector S3) checks that the batch a newer batch SUPERSEDED holds its validation and close artifacts. THE REFUSAL IS THE DELIVERABLE: batch-88 (defect) and batch-89 (correct) are identical in every field a local rule can read -- both merged, both at P3, both missing 04-validation.md and 05-close.md -- so a rule keyed on 'merged below P4' is RED TODAY ON CORRECT WORK, which is C-53's false fail and worse than no rule; a rule that cries wolf is how people learn to ignore the gate. What separates them is SUPERSESSION, and V28's three costs are written into its own block comment: it fires one station late, it never looks at a commit, and it has a one-batch window bought with a measurement (of 72 batch-shaped directories, NINE hold neither or only one closing artifact -- batches 25, 63, 66, 71, 73, 75, 78, 79, 85 -- so a corpus-wide sweep would print nine notices about closed history at every gate forever). MEASURED AT THE COMMIT: 490 arms (443 -> 490), SELFTEST PASSED; 24 -> 26 registered rules; 47 V27/V28 arms ok; V26 on this record 41,060 chars inside the 54,000 budget, no strikethrough, 22 pairings identical both ways. 25 named single-edit mutants: 24 killed, 1 survived, 0 broken, each scored against the run's own baseline with the kill criterion being the SET of failing arm labels growing. THREE THINGS THAT WENT WRONG INSIDE THE MUTATION PASS, all recorded rather than tidied: the first baseline came back RED because the interpreter increment's INT FOUR-PLACES-agree walks up from __file__ and reports the layout outside a flow-shaped tree, so the battery moved to a MIRRORED flow tree -- a baseline that is already red cannot score anything, and lowering the bar would have been the vacuous check one level out; M13-nodate-silent was REWRITTEN BECAUSE IT WAS BROKEN, not because it survived, having crashed at 454 arms with no verdict line, which reads exactly like a survivor; and the one survivor M15-zero-padding-dropped is recorded EQUIVALENT BY EXECUTION rather than chased, because no input separates the two forms. TWO FINDINGS THE LIVE GATE RAISED THE MOMENT THE RULES SHIPPED, BOTH TRUE AND BOTH SHIPPED UNREPAIRED: R-89-9, this decisions_log was never reset when batch-89 opened and still held batch-88's ten entries while batch_id read 2026-08-28-batch-89; and R-89-10, the unimplementable property itself. ABSENT: the gate line at this commit was not recorded and the batch has no 04-validation.md to hold it. Packet: 03-increments/increment-006.md, WRITTEN 2026-08-30, hours after the commit.

decisions_log.notes: REPAIR OF R-89-9, WHICH THIS BATCH REGISTERED AND SHIPPED OPEN. Before this edit the log held batch-88's ten entries, dated 2026-08-24 to 2026-08-27, while batch_id read 2026-08-28-batch-89 and the batch directory held ZERO increment packets. V27, shipped hours earlier by this same batch, reported both halves against it: '2 decisions_log decision(s) name an increment with no packet on disk -- increment(s) 1, 2' and 'the newest decisions_log entry is dated 2026-08-27 while the newest commit touching the batch directory is dated 2026-08-30'. Both findings were TRUE and their subject was the ROLLOVER, not the rule. WHAT HAPPENED TO batch-88's TEN ENTRIES: they were REPLACED, not merged and not archived here, because the per-batch convention is real and measured -- batch-88's own log at its merge carries NOT ONE batch-87 entry (P-13). Nothing is lost: the ten entries are byte-identical at 0f40624 (batch-88's merge) and at 686733c (this branch's tip before this edit), verified by loading both with json and comparing the lists, and they are also narrated in batch-88's own 04-validation.md and 05-close.md, both of which were themselves written retroactively on 2026-08-29 and say so at the top. WHAT WAS NOT INVENTED: no P0, ARQ, P1 or PDR entry was written for batch-89, because no such decision is recorded anywhere in this batch's record and a plausible entry is worse than an absent one. The four entries above are exactly the four increments that have packets on disk. WHAT WAS NOT TOUCHED, and it is stale: batch_objective still names the budget as 55000 -- the figure LED-89.5 refuted the same day, superseding it to 54,000 computed rather than typed -- and still lists two shipped increments under 'REMAINING INCREMENTS, NOT IMPLEMENTED'; artifact_homes and triggers.record still point at .dev-flow/2026-08-24-batch-88/, including artifact_homes.increments, which names batch-88's 03-increments while this batch now has its own; and current_station, phase_status, stations_active and iterations_per_station were never reset either. This write was scoped to decisions_log, and expanding it silently would be the scope creep this flow forbids, so the staleness is reported here rather than repaired. THE PACKETS ARE RETROACTIVE AND EVERY ONE OF THEM SAYS SO WITH ITS DATE. They are transcription and reconciliation of figures taken during the work -- from the three landing commits, from FLOW-VERSION.md's rev48, rev49 and rev50 rows, and from the batch's own ledger; nothing in them was re-measured at rev50 and presented as the work's own, and where evidence does not exist the field is marked ABSENT with the reason. NO code-reviewer VERDICT EXISTS FOR ANY OF THE FOUR INCREMENTS; batch-88 ran that lens at every increment and this batch ran it at none, and the packets say so rather than implying otherwise.
